newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak due to arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak due to arbitrage.

text.p: The Philippine peso was pulled down on Friday by the usual arbitrage play for the weekend, traders said.
It closed at 26.380 to the dollar, down from 26.372, with volume lower at $397.7 million from $529.5 million.

Banks usually sell dollars for same-day delivery to earn the higher interest offered by the peso for the coming weekend. At the same time, they also buy dollars for settlement on Monday which brings down the peso due to the interest differential.
"The trend was to sell dollars because of the high overnight rate," one trader said.
On Thursday, the Central Bank lifted its key overnight borrowing rate by 2.25 percentage points to 15 percent to fend off speculation against the spillover of Thailand's financial woes.
Though the peso stayed within a narrow band of 26.378/26.383, trades were still heavy as some banks also tried to cover dollars they shorted yesterday due to the rate increase, traders said.
"There was good buying on dollars," a second trader said.
"The tone for next week will still be biddish on the dollar," he added, because Thailand's problems may not yet be over.
Nevertheless, another said the peso managed to calm down today. "There were dollar inflows," he said.
In late trades, dealers said they saw the Central Bank buying about $34 million to $52 million at 26.380/26.382 in order to replenish the dollars they sold on Thursday.
Traders had estimated the Central Bank had sold about $200 million yesterday before announcing the rate increase at midday.
"He (the Central Bank) needs to replenish his dollars. He knows he may have to sell dollars again," a dealer said.
